sentences.text: Serbia's president quit to run for prime minister. Weeks later, he lost to a list backed by students.
Who can vote? Citizens aged 18 who live in Serbia. Living abroad? Sign up first.
Circle the number of one party list. And your finger gets invisible ink, so no one votes twice.
The whole country is one district: lists above 3% share 250 seats. Minority parties don't need the 3%.
That's the National Assembly: it makes laws, passes the budget and elects the government.
The prime minister, proposed by the president, needs 126 votes: a majority.
The president is elected directly, with a run-off if no one gets half, and can send laws back, but not block them.
In October 2026, the Student List won 140 seats, and Vučić's list 104.
And a new president is due by December. Can a movement with no clear leader run a country?
